message.content:
Yes—if you’re experiencing excessive or disruptive noise in Atlanta, you can file a complaint with the city’s authorities. In most cases, the City of Atlanta’s **Department of Public Safety** (or the local police department) handles noise complaints. Here’s how you can do it:

| Step | What to Do | Contact Info |
|------|------------|--------------|
| 1 | Identify the source of the noise (e.g., a neighbor’s party, construction, loud music). | N/A |
| 2 | Gather details: address, time, duration, and any evidence (photos, videos, audio recordings). | N/A |
| 3 | Call the Atlanta Police Department’s non-emergency line at **404‑656‑4000** (for general noise complaints). | 404‑656‑4000 |
| 4 | Alternatively, you can file a complaint online through the City of Atlanta’s official portal: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> (select “Noise” under “Report a Problem”). | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> |
| 5 | If the issue involves a business or commercial property, you may also contact the **Atlanta Office of Code Enforcement** at **404‑656‑4000** or via email at **code.enforcement@atlantaga.gov**. | 404‑656‑4000 / code.enforcement@atlantaga.gov |

### Quick Tips

- **Non-Emergency Line:** Use 404‑656‑4000 only if the situation isn’t urgent (i.e., not a crime in progress). For emergencies, dial 911.
- **Online Reporting:** The 311 portal allows you to attach photos or videos directly to your submission, which can help investigators assess the situation more quickly.
- **Follow Up:** After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. Keep it handy if you need to follow up or request updates on the investigation.

If you’re dealing with a recurring problem or suspect a violation of the city’s noise ordinance, the city’s code enforcement officers will investigate and may issue citations or fines if the complaint is substantiated.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like more detailed guidance on the noise ordinance itself or how to prepare documentation for your complaint!
